<reason>Both sides argued at a high level with disciplined, closed-book reasoning. A built a genuinely sharp case ("aggressive" at scale means automation; false positives are regressive, hitting invested accounts and bouncing off throwaways; mass-report weaponization) and its answer to B's contradiction question ("both, for different people — that asymmetry is the point") was one of the strongest moments in the debate. But A's route had two self-inflicted wounds that B exploited well: A's own alternative included report-driven quarantine matchmaking, which B correctly showed "inherits every flaw CON attributes to mine" and is itself a behavior-based verdict imposed over the same culture objections; and A conceded that mute/block does nothing against a fifty-account doxxing pile-on, then had to import friction measures late while quietly re-describing quarantine as merely grouping new accounts. B also landed the cleanest decision rule: the motion is normative, so "publishers won't pay" concedes the principle and argues only the invoice, and "whose risk does the platform carry when unsure" is answered by the asymmetry between the veteran with an appeal and the silent, uncounted exit. B additionally narrowed the target early (slurs, threats, sexual harassment, doxxing, pile-ons — not banter), which turns much of A's false-positive case into an implementation caveat rather than a reason to reject the motion; A's rejoinder that severe cases are "already at ten" everywhere was asserted rather than established. A's best late hit — that B's triage sends humans to already-enforced severe cases and machines to the ambiguous middle — was real and B's closing did not answer it squarely, which keeps this competitive rather than lopsided. Three clipped over-limit turns for A is a further execution cost. On balance B made the choice easier to decide.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's turn on A's own remedies: quarantine matchmaking is report-driven sorting, so it "is a verdict with a friendlier interface" and inherits the very unreliability A blames on aggressive enforcement — paired with the pile-on question A had to answer with "no button helps."</best_rebuttal>
